Tax uses **banker's rounding (`decimal.ROUND_HALF_EVEN`)**, never `ROUND_HALF_UP`. Round the tax on each line item separately, then add up the rounded line taxes. Don't round the invoice total.

This comes from a team memory recording a March 2026 decision made with the finance team, after customers reported invoices that were off by a cent. A related rule says every money amount is integer cents using the `Money` type in `src/billing/money.py`, with no floats anywhere, even in intermediate math.

The code doesn't implement this yet. `tax_for` in `src/billing/tax.py:11` just raises `NotImplementedError`, and `tests/test_tax.py` only tests `line_total`. So the rule exists only in the memory, not in code or tests. If you implement `tax_for`, it should apply `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` to each line's tax in cents. I can write it and add tests for the half-cent cases if you'd like.
